identity.title: DepthLM: Metric Depth from Vision Language Models

problem.claim: Can vision-language models achieve expert-level metric depth accuracy without changing their architecture or loss?

gap.claim: VLMs excel at semantic understanding but struggle with 3D understanding from 2D inputs, while high-accuracy pure vision models require task-specific architectures and losses.

contributions.claim: DepthLM uses text-based supervised fine-tuning with sparse labels, visual prompting, and intrinsic-conditioned augmentation for metric depth estimation.
The authors identify pixel reference and cross-dataset camera ambiguity as bottlenecks for VLM-based metric depth estimation.
The proposed approach is designed to let one VLM cover multiple 3D tasks beyond metric depth.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that DepthLM makes VLMs comparable with pure vision models for metric depth for the first time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that text-based supervised fine-tuning with sparse labels is sufficient to unlock strong 3D understanding, without a dense prediction head or complex regression/regularization loss.
The authors report that, with much smaller models, DepthLM surpasses the accuracy of most advanced VLMs by over 2×.
The authors report that DepthLM makes VLMs comparable with pure vision models.

narrative_sequence.summary: VLMs flexibly address vision tasks through text, but struggle with 3D understanding from 2D inputs.
Pure vision models achieve super-human metric-depth accuracy but depend on task-specific architectures and losses, motivating an architecture- and loss-preserving alternative.
DepthLM uses sparse-label text supervision and addresses pixel reference and camera ambiguity through visual prompting and intrinsic-conditioned augmentation.
The authors report more than 2× higher accuracy than most advanced VLMs with much smaller models, plus coverage of additional 3D tasks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a simple training setup to two diagnosed bottlenecks—pixel reference and cross-dataset camera ambiguity—and names targeted remedies for each.

lessons.interpretation: A compact problem-to-intervention mapping can make a method’s design rationale legible without detailing every component.
lessons.application: When presenting a new multimodal method, explicitly pair each identified bottleneck with the mechanism intended to address it.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when bottlenecks have not been isolated or when one mechanism affects several coupled failure modes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, metrics, evaluation protocols, or what 'over 2×' measures.
The meanings of 'sparse labels,' 'most advanced VLMs,' 'super-human,' and 'comparable' are not operationalized.
The abstract does not provide evidence for the claimed first-time distinction beyond the authors' statement.
